QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_9

question.text: Ujala Solar Pvt Ltd claims its off-grid solar lamps created 5,000 new jobs in rural Bihar. The SIA discovers that 1,500 of those jobs came at the direct expense of local kerosene retailers who closed down. In SROI, how should the 1,500 jobs be treated?

answer.text: Added as additional positive outcome — job creation is always positive
Treated as displacement — deducted from gross outcome because the job was transferred from one group to another, not net-new
Treated as drop-off — because kerosene retailers dropped out
Treated as deadweight — because the market would have shifted anyway

explanation.text: The Logic: In SROI terminology, "displacement" is the portion of an apparent outcome that has merely been transferred from one group to another rather than created as net-new value. Here, 1,500 of the 5,000 newly created solar-related jobs came at the direct expense of kerosene retailers who closed down - those jobs are a substitution, not a net social gain. To avoid over-stating impact, the SROI calculation must deduct that displaced portion from the gross outcome before computing the ratio. The Trap: Treating the 1,500 jobs as additional positive outcome (option A) double-counts and overstates impact. Drop-off (option C) is about an outcome fading over time, not about an outcome being substituted from another group; the kerosene retailers were displaced, not subject to temporal decay. Deadweight (option D) refers to the share of the outcome that would have happened anyway in the absence of the intervention - it captures the counterfactual baseline, not a substitution between groups. Note: The cited workbook pages (134, 151, 157, 158 of the Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook) support the general SROI ideas of checking what would have happened absent the project and of identifying unintended impacts, but they do not, in the pages checked, define "displacement" as the substitution of one group's outcome for another's, or state that transferred jobs should be deducted from gross outcome. The framing above reflects general SROI methodology as practised in social-impact evaluation.
